name: Peak Shift
tagline: Run things when power is cheap, and cut the standby
about: Peak Shift works out what each appliance really costs to run, builds a daily plan to shift washing, dishwashing, charging and heating into off-peak or solar hours, checks whether a time-of-use tariff would pay, and hunts down phantom standby loads.
persona: You are a pragmatic home-energy analyst: every claim comes with a kWh number, you respect that people won't rewire their lives, and you never sell gadgets.

onboarding.title: Same life, cheaper hours
onboarding.subtitle: Your tariff and appliances make the numbers real.
bullets: Cost per cycle for every appliance

tools.title: What does it cost to run?
tools.subtitle: Wattage or rating plate → cost per use

inputs.label: Photo of the rating plate or energy label
Appliance and use
inputs.placeholder: tumble dryer, 5 loads a week; or 2000W kettle

tools.prompt: Using the photo if given and '{appliance}' with the profile rates: kv (power draw kW, energy per use kWh, cost per use at peak, cost per use off-peak, cost per year at current use), a table (Alternative | kWh per use | Saving per year) such as heat-pump dryer, airing rack or eco mode, and a callout on the assumptions made about wattage and cycle length.

tools.title: Shift my day
tools.subtitle: When to run everything for the cheapest day

inputs.label: What runs in a typical day
inputs.placeholder: dishwasher nightly, washing 4x/week, EV charge 20kWh Tue/Thu, immersion heater, gaming PC evenings

tools.prompt: Build a load-shifting plan for the profile tariff for: {loads}. Table (Appliance | Run at | Delay-start setting | Weekly kWh | Weekly cost now | After shift), kv (weekly saving, yearly saving, what can't move), steps to set delay timers and smart plugs once, and a callout on fire safety for running appliances overnight (dryers, dishwashers, chargers).

tools.title: Would a different tariff pay?
tools.subtitle: Time-of-use, EV or solar-export tariffs

inputs.label: Usage and habits
inputs.placeholder: 3,400 kWh/yr, EV, home in evenings, could shift washing

inputs.label: Tariff you're considering
inputs.placeholder: peak 35p 4–7pm, off-peak 12p overnight, same standing charge

tools.prompt: Compare the profile's current tariff with '{offer}' for: {usage}. Table (Scenario | Annual cost current | Annual cost new | Difference) for 'no change in habits', 'shift the easy loads' and 'shift everything possible', kv (break-even share of usage off-peak, biggest lever), bullets on the questions to ask before switching (exit fees, smart-meter requirement, price-cap rules), and a callout stating the estimate assumptions.

tools.title: Standby hunt
tools.subtitle: Find the phantom loads worth killing

inputs.label: Devices left plugged in
inputs.placeholder: TV + soundbar, 2 consoles, router, printer, phone chargers, coffee machine on clock

tools.prompt: Estimate standby for: {devices}. Table (Device | Standby W est. | Cost per year | Kill it? yes / no / smart plug), kv (total standby cost per year, saving if the yes-items are switched off, payback on a smart plug strip), a checklist of what to switch off tonight, and a callout on what must stay on (router if needed, fridge, boiler controls, security).

tools.title: Use my own solar
tools.subtitle: Self-consumption with or without a battery
tools.prompt: For '{system}' with forecast '{day}': steps for tomorrow's running order timed to the sun (washing, dishwasher, immersion, EV, cooking), a table (Hour | Expected generation kW est. | Run this), kv (self-consumption % achievable, value of export versus using it yourself), and a callout on whether a battery or diverter would pay for this setup with a rough payback range.

disclaimer: Estimates only; check figures with your supplier and meter, and never modify wiring or overload sockets — use a qualified electrician.
